recipes.title: Savory Egg Custard Pots Udo And Chicken Steamed With Sour Plums
recipes.transcription:
Preparation time: 20 minutes
Cooking
time: 30 minutes
Serves: 4
1% cups (13
fl oz/ 400 ml) Katsuobushi
Dashi (page 156)
2 teaspoons
usukuchi shoyu
• I teaspoon mirin
¼ teaspoon fine sea salt
2 eggs,
at room temperature
3 small
sh ii take, stems discarded
3 1/2 oz (100 g) boneless, skinless
chicken breast
2 tablespoons soy
sauce
6 shrimp (prawns), peeled and
deveined
4 slices ('/• inch / 6
mm) kamaboko [fish
cake). halved
crosswise
12 ginkgo
nuts , shelled and skinned
• I small handful mitsuba, sliced
crosswise into %-inch (2 cm)
pieces
• ½ teaspoon finely slivered yuzu zest
Preparation time: 15 minutes
Cooking time: 5 minutes
Serves: 6
2% oz
(75 g) udo or celery
II oz (300 g) boneless , skinless
chicken breast
6 tablespoons Katsuobushi Dashi
(page 156)
3 tablespoons sake
½ tablespoon soy sauce
• ½ tablespoon mirin
3 small umeboshi
[salted sour plum],
pitted and torn into
small pieces
SAVORY EGG CUSTARD POTS
Considering the moving parts
to this version of chawan mushi,
you might want to double the
recipe when friends are coming
for dinner.
In a saucepan, stir the dashi, usukuchi
sh'!)'u, mirin, and salt over medium­
low heat until the salt has dissolved.
Cool. In a large glass measuring
cup ~ug) with a
spout, whisk the
eggs , without letting them foam
up , and slowly whisk in the cooled ,
flavored dashi.
In a small pot of salted boiling
water , blanch the shiitake for
30 seconds. Pat the caps dry in
a clean tea towel, and quarter.
Cut the chicken on the bias into
'/•-inch (6
mm) wide pieces. Toss
with the soy sauce, then blot dry
with absorbent paper towels.
Divide the shiitake, chicken , shrimp ,
kamaboko, ginkgo nuts, and mitsuba
(reserving a few of the nicest leaves
for garnish) among four
7 fl oz
(200 ml) chawan mushi
or handleless teacups (preferably
with lids). Give the egg mixture one
more quick whisk and pour into the
cups , leaving ½ inch (12 mm) free
at the
top to allow for expansion.
Place the lids on the cups (or cover
with plastic wrap [clingfilm]) .
Set up a steamer and bring the
water to a boil. Arrange the cups
in the steamer basket, cover, and
steam for 20-25 minutes. Sprinkle
with the yu-tti zest, a few mitsuba
leaves , and serve hot.
[Qj p.193
UDO AND CHICKEN STEAMED
WITH SOUR PLUMS
Udo is a mountain vegetable similar
in texture to celery but with a
unique bitter, earthy flavor. Seek
it out if possible.
Peel the udo and cut lengthwise
into '/•- inch (6 mm) slices.
Cut
those slices crosswise into 11/+-inch
(3 cm) pieces . If substituting with
celery , slice crosswise at a diagonal
into '/•- inch (6
mm) pieces. Cut
the chicken into bite-size pieces by
slicing into the chicken meat with
your knife at a 45-degree angle
(sogigiri, see page).
In a medium saucepan , combine
the chicken pieces and udo and
measure in the dashi, sake, soy sauce,
and mirin. The liquid should come
about one-third of the way up
the sides of the chicken and udo.
If it doesn't, add in a little more
sake. Add the umeboshi. Bring to
a boil over high heat, ad just to a
simmer , and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Immediately
remove the saucepan
from the heat.
Let cool completely in the pan
before serving.
192 MUSHIMONO - STEAMED

recipes.title: Chrysanthemum Petal­ Steamed Fish Balls Steamed Onions With Bacon
recipes.transcription:
Preparation time: 30 minutes
Cooking time: 15 minutes
Makes: 12 small balls
IO oz (300 g) white fish fillet (such as
snapper, flounder , halibut, or swordfish)
I small egg white, at room temperature
• I tablespoon sake
I tablespoon plus 2 teaspoons
potato starch
2 pinches of freshly ground
black pepper
1¾ oz
(50 g) chrysanthemum flowers,
about 12
I teaspoon canola (rapeseed) oil
% cup (5 fl oz/r50 ml) Katsuobushi
Dashi
(page 156)
¼ teaspoon fine sea salt
• I small handful shungiku
[chrysanthemum leaves], for garnish
Preparation time : 15 minutes
Cooking time: 15 minutes
Serves : 6
5 oz (150 g) sliced unsmoked bacon,
cut crosswise into pieces I½ inches
(4 cm) wide
I medium onion, halved and thinly
sliced crosswise
5 oz (150 g) green cabbage , sliced
crosswise into 1 1/+-inch (3 cm) pieces
· 2½ oz (75 g) enoki mushrooms ,
halved crosswise
• Japanese Rice (page 291), for serving
•½lemon
CHRYSANTHEMUM PETAL­
STEAMED FISH BALLS
Bright yellow from the
chrysanthemum flowers, these
fish balls are stunning and simple
to make . Serve as a first course.
Dice the fish and pound to a paste
in a suribachi [grinding bowl] or
food processor. Mash in the egg
white, sake, I tablespoon of the
potato starch, and I pinch of black
pepper. Dampen your palms with
cold water, divide the fish paste
into
12 portions , and
roll into
small balls . Line the balls up on
a piece of parchment paper. Strew
the chrysanthemum flowers across
the bottom of a shallow pan. Drop
one fish ball at a time in the pan
and roll it around by tilting the pan
so that the petals have completely
covered the surface of the fish balls
and are well adhered.
Set up a steamer and bring the
water to a boil. Measure the oil
onto a plate, roll the balls gently in
the oil, and place the plate in the
steamer basket. Cover and steam
until set, 12-15 minutes.
In a small saucepan, heat the
dashi,
salt, and remaining pinch of black
pepper. In a small bowl, dissolve
the remaining 2 teaspoons potato
starch in 2 tablespoons water. Stir
the potato starch slurry into the
dashi and cook over low heat until
glossy, and slightly thickened ,
1-2 minutes .
To serve, arrange a few shungiku
artfully on a pretty dinner plate ,
spoon the fish balls onto the plate
in one layer , and nap with the
thickened dashi. Serve hot.
[Q] p .195
STEAMED ONIONS WITH BACON
Japanese bacon is thinly sliced,
unsmoked, and does not contain
much fat. For this method, try
to find a similar style of bacon.
Arrange half of the bacon across
the surface of a large frying pan.
Scatter the onion slices across the
bacon. Top with the cabbage, then
the enoki, and the other half of
the bacon . Cover and cook over
medium-high heat until the heat
reaches through to cook the top
pieces of bacon, and the vegetables
release some of their juices,
10-15 minutes .
Spoon
onto individual bowls of hot
rice with a squeeze of fresh lemon
juice. Keeps well as a leftover,
though keep the layers intact for
a neat presentation. Reheat before
serving .
194 MUSHIMONO - STEAMED

recipes.title: Sour Plum-Steamed Cod Steamed Mountain Yam With Nori
recipes.transcription:
Preparation time: 40 minutes
Cooking time: 15 minutes
Serves: 6
• I lb 2 oz (500 g) cod fillet, skinned
• ½ teaspoon flaky sea salt
• 4 tablespoons sake
3
umeboshi [salted sour plum]. pitted
and finely chopped to a paste, or
I tablespoon sour plum paste
• 2 medium
negi or 8 fat scalli ons
(spring onions), sliced into 2-inch
(5
cm) pieces
I teaspoon soy sauce
½ teaspoon potato starch, thinned with
I tablespoon water
Preparation time: 30 minutes
Cooking time: 20 minutes
Serves:
6-8
14 oz (400 g) naga imo [mountain
yam). peeled
4 chicken
tenders (sasami) or
I (ro½ oz/300 g) boneless, skinless
chicken breast
• I teaspoon flaky sea salt
· 2 tablespoons sake
Generous
r½ cups (4 1/2 oz/r25 g)
edamame
pods, boiled for 3 minutes
and
shelled
• I lily bulb, brown parts pared off,
"petals" separated
• 4 shiitake,
stems discarded and caps
quartered
• % cup (5 fl oz/r50 ml) Konbu Dashi
(page 156), at room temperature
• I tablespoon usukuchi shoyu
I sheet nori, snipped into fine threads
• Japanese Rice (page 291), for serving
(optional)
SOUR PLUM-STEAMED COD
Cod, commonly available in Japan,
takes well to steaming. The umeboshi
[salted sour plum) introduces a
bright note to the slightly mild
quality of this fish, while the
caramelized negi adds sweetness.
Cut the cod fillet in half, arrange
on a plate that will fit into a steamer
(I0-12 inches/25-30 cm across),
sprinkle with the salt on both sides,
and moisten with the
sake. Let sit
for 30 minutes.
Set up the steamer and bring the
water to a boil. Spread a thin layer
of umeboshi paste on the stomach side
(as opposed to the skinned side) of
the fish and lower the plate into the
steamer basket. Cover and steam
over medium heat for IO minutes.
While the cod is steaming, in a
dry heavy frying pan, pan-grill the
negi, covered, over low heat. Keep
close watch and turn the pieces as
you check periodically. Take care
not to burn. Transfer to a small
plate when softened and slightly
caramelized, 7-10 minutes.
Remove the plate with the fish from
the steamer carefully so as not to
lose the precious juices. Pour the
hot juices into a small saucepan and
season with the soy sauce. Whisk in
the potato starch, simmer gently
over low heat for 2 minutes.
Pour
the sauce back over the fish. Wipe
the edges and bottom of the plate
to clean up any drips or residual
steaming liquid. Strew the negi on
the plate and serve.
[Q] p.197
STEAMED MOUNTAIN YAM
WITH NORI
Once steamed, grated noga imo
[mountain yam) sets and becomes
almost creamy. The colors and
textures in this dish are lovely.
Finely grate the noga imo on an
oroshigane U apanese grating plate) to
form a viscous mass.
Cut the sasami crosswise into thirds.
(If using chicken breast, cut in
thirds lengthwise , and then again
crosswise in thirds.)
Lay a 2-foot (60 cm) piece of foil
out on your workspace. Place the
chicken pieces in the middle of
the foil in one layer. Sprinkle
with ½ teaspoon of the salt and
I tablespoon of the sake. Fold the
foil up to make a tight package
(taking care that the chicken pieces
remain in one laye r).
Set up a steamer and bring the
water to a boil. Place the foil
packet in the steamer ba sket, cover,
and steam for 5 minutes. Remove
the steamer basket but keep the
water hot.
Open the packet and let the
chicken cool in its juices for
IO minutes before cutting into
%-inch (1.5 cm) cubes. Arrange
the half-cooked chicken pieces
in an 8 - inch (20 cm)
round or
square pan with the edamame, lily
"peta ls ", and shiitake. Measure
in the dashi, usukuchi sh'D'u, the
remaining ½ teaspoon salt, and
I tablespoon sake. Slurp the grated
naga imo over the surface. Set in the
steamer basket, cover, and steam
for 15 minutes. Strew with nori and
serve as is, or spooned over rice.
MU SHIM ONO - STEAMED

recipes.title: Cold Steamed Chicken Stuffed Kabocha Mu Shim Ono - Steamed
recipes.transcription:
Preparation time: IO minutes
Cooking time, 20 minutes
Serves, 4
2 boneless , skinless
chicken breasts
(8 oz/225 g each)
I teaspoon flaky sea salt
· 2 tablespoons sake
2 tablespoons rice vinegar
• 2 tablespoons
mirin
2 tablespoons
soy sauce
1/2 teaspoon mustard powder
Preparation time, 40 minutes
Cooking time, I hour
Serves , 6
I (ro½ oz / 300 g) momendofu or
Japanese-style soft block tofu
I (3 lb / r.35 kg) medium kabocha
(Japanese pumpkin)
2 teaspoons
flaky sea salt
4 small
dried shiitake, soaked in boiling
water for 30 minutes
I small carrot, scrubbed and
finely diced
½ lb (225 g) finely ground (minced)
chicken
I tablespoon mirin
1 1/, cup (ro fl oz/300 ml) Japanese
Chicken
Broth (page 160)
· 2 teaspoons
soy sauce
I teaspoon potato starch dissolved in
I tablespoon water
COLD STEAMED CHICKEN
Having a couple of cold cooked
chicken breasts on hand, to toss
into salads or add to dressed
vegetables, turns a side dish into a
meal. Steaming with sake means that
the chicken meat does not dry out,
making it a useful technique to have
in your repertoire . You can serve
the chicken shredded or sliced,
depending on your preference.
Pull off 2 large
pieces of foil and
lay them across your workspace .
Set one chicken breast on each
piece of foil and salt evenly on
both sides. Sprinkle each breast
with I tablespoon sake and fold the
foil ends up together. Roll down
and scrunch closed to make
a tight package.
Set up a steamer and bring the
water to a boil. Arrange the packets
in the steamer basket, cover, and
steam for about 20 minutes .
Remove
from the heat to cool.
Serve the chicken simply , with a
dressing, In a bowl , whisk together
the vinegar , mirin, and soy sauce.
Whisk that mixture slowly into the
mustard powder . Dress the chicken
and serve immediately.
[Qj P-199
STUFFED KABOCHA
Stuffed kabocha (Japanese
pumpkin) is excellent for a crowd
or even for a small dinner.
Set the tofu on a cutting board and
prop a small saucer underneath it
to angle the board into the kitchen
sink (to catch drips). Lay another
cutting board on top of the tofu to
press out moisture for 20 minutes.
Cut the top off the kabocha with
a heavy butcher knife by inserting
the knife diagonally into the skin
to cut out a reusable top
(like when
carving
a pumpkin for Halloween).
Scoop out the seeds and s crape the
lingering threads out with a spoon.
Massage I teaspoon of the salt into
the inside flesh of the pumpkin.
Drain the shiitake, discard the stems,
and finely dice
the caps. Squeeze the
tofu by handfuls to remove any last
moisture and drop into a medium
bowl. Add the diced shiitake, carrot,
chicken, remaining I teaspoon
salt, and mirin and mix with saibashi
[cooking chopsticks) until all
of th e ingredient s are evenly
incorporated. Stuff the mixture
into the kabocha . Press down to
eliminate air pockets but do not
overwork the meat mixture.
Set up a steamer (large enough to
accommodate the kabocha) and
bring the water to a boil. Place the
stuffed kabocha and the lid side
by side in the steamer , cover. and
steam until the meat filling is well
set , about I hour.
In a saucepan, combine the chicken
broth and soy sauce and bring to
a simmer over medium-high heat.
Scrape in the potato starch mixture
and simmer gently until slightly
thickened , 2-3 minutes .
Remove the kabocha from the
steamer and set on platter. Place
the steamed lid on top , pour the
sauce over the kabocha, and serve
by slicing into large wedges .
MU SHIM ONO - STEAMED

recipes.title: Chicken And Vegetable Stuffed Kabocha 200 Mushimono - Steamed
recipes.transcription:
Preparation time: I hour
Cooking time: I hour
Serves: 6
I (ro½ oz / 300 g) momendofu or
Japanese-style soft block tofu
I (3 lb/1.35 kg) medium kabocha
(Japanese pumpkin)
13/+ teaspoons
fine sea salt
2 ½ tablespoons potato starch
(1% oz/ 50
g) naga imo [mountain yam]
• I small carrot , scrubbed and diced
5 oz (145 g) burdock root, scrubbed
and diced
2 medium shiitake caps, diced
• 5 oz (150 g) finely ground
(minced) chicken
½ tablespoon organic powdered
chicken or vegetable bouillon
1% cups (14 fl
oz/ 400 ml) Kon
bu
Dashi (page 156)
½ tablespoon soy sauce
• ½ teaspoon flaky sea salt
• % cup
(2½ oz/75 g) green peas,
parboiled for 2-3 minutes
until soft
but not mushy
CHICKEN AND VEGETABLE
STUFFED KABOCHA
The presentation here is stunning
because the stuffed kabocha (Japanese
pumpkin) is steamed whole and
served with a silky sauce studded with
green peas.
Set the tofu on a cutting board and
prop a small saucer underneath
to angle the board into the kitchen
sink (to catch drips) . Lay another
cutting board on top of the tofu to
press out moisture for 20 minutes.
In sert a heavy, sharp knife at a
diagonal into the top flesh around
the stem area of the kabocha to cut
out a 4-inch (ro cm) round
lid .
Scoop out the seeds and scrape any
lingering threads off the inside of the
kabocha lid. Rub I½ teaspoons of the
fine salt into all surfaces of kabocha
cavity. Sprinkle the cavity with
2 tablespoons of the potato starch.
Drop the pressed tofu into a
suribachi [grinding bowl] and
emulsify with a surikogi [ wooden
pestle] using circular, grinding
motions. (Alternatively , smash in
a medium bowl.) Grate the naga imo
on an oroshigane Uapanese grating
plate] and incorporate into the
tofu with the surikogi. Fold in the
carrot, burdock, shiitake, chicken,
and powdered bouillon. Pack the
mixture into the kabocha, sprinkle
the remaining 'I• teaspoon fine salt
onto the inside of the lid and fit it
back on top of the kabocha.
Set up a large steamer (one that
can accommodate the kabocha) and
bring the water to a boil. Add the
kabocha to the steamer basket and
steam until the stuffing has set and
the kabocha is cooked through, but
not collapsing , about 60 minutes.
In a small bowl , dissolve the
remaining ½ tablespoon potato
starch in 2 tablespoons cold water.
In a saucepan, combine the
dashi,
soy sauce , and flaky salt and heat
over medium-high heat, stirring
to dissolve the salt. Sprinkle in the
green peas and the potato starch
slurry and simmer 2-3 minutes
to
make a silky, thin glaze for the
stuffed kabocha.
Present the steamed kabocha on
an attractive rimmed dinner plate
with the lid propped up beside it.
Drizzle the thickened dashi over the
kabocha so it spills out prettily onto
the plate. Slice into wedges and
serve . It holds up very well to the
next day, if stored refrigerated.
200 MUSHIMONO - STEAMED

recipes.title: Steamed Grated Turnip Mushimono - Steamed
recipes.transcription:
Preparation time: 30 minutes
Cooking time, 15 minutes
Serves, 6
For
the custard,
5¼ oz (150 g) turnips scrubbed and
finely grated
4
sasami [chicken tenders) or
l (4½ oz/225 g) boneless, skinless
chicken breast
1¾ oz (50 g) awafu [wheat gluten with
millet) or fresh yuba
½ teaspoon flaky sea salt
l small lily bulb, brown spots pared off,
"petals" separated
12 ginkgo
nuts, shelled and skinned
(see Note)
2 tablespoons mirin
3 small dried shiitake , soaked in boiling
water for 30 minutes, drained, stems
discarded , and caps thinly sliced
Q eggs, at room temperature
For the sauce:
• 1¼ cups (ro fl oz/300 ml)
Katsuobushi Dashi (page 156)
• l tablespoon potato starch
l tablespoon usukuchi shoyu
½ teaspoon fine sea
salt
· l tablespoon mirin
• 2 tablespoons sake
l tablespoon slivered yuzu zest
STEAMED GRATED TURNIP
This classic dish is usually seen as
a one - dish meal , but here the small
presentation makes it easier to
serve . For leftovers, reheat the pots
in a steamer and the creamy sauce
in a small pan over low heat.
Make the custard, Scrape the grated
turnip into a fine mesh sieve to
drain. Slice the chicken tenders
against the grain into %-inch
(1.5 cm) cubes. If using awafa, cut
into %-inch (1.5 cm) squares;
if usingyuba , cut crosswise into
%-inch (1. 5 cm) sections. Massage
the flaky salt into the lily "petals"
and ginkgo nuts in a medium bowl.
Drizzle in the mirin.
Divide the "petals" and ginkgo nuts
evenly among six 5 '/• fl
oz (150 ml)
chawan mushi or handleless teacups .
Drop some shiitake, chicken, awafu
(or yuba) into each of the cups.
Crack the eggs into a medium bowl
and whisk to emulsify . Whisk in
the drained grated turnip until
incorporated with the egg. Pour
into the cups and place their lids
on (or cover tightly with foil).
Set up a steamer and bring the
water to a boil. Arrange the custard
cups in the steamer, cover, and
steam over medium-low heat for
15 minutes.
Make
the sauce, In a small
bowl,
stir a little bit of the dashi into the
potato starc h to make a slurry. In
a saucepan, combine the remaining
dashi, usukuchi sh'?)'u, salt, mirin, and
sake and heat to a simmer over
medium heat. Stir in the potato
starch slurry and simmer gently
for I-2 minutes , stirring, until the
sauce is silky smooth but not goopy.
To serve, remove the custards from
the steamer and serve hot with the
sauce ladled in , and sprinkled with
slivered yuzu zest.
Note, Place
the ginkgo nuts in a
medium saucepan , fill with
cold
water to cover by ¾ inch (2 cm) ,
add 2 teaspoons salt, and bring
to a boil over high heat. Boil for
IO minutes. Drain and refresh
under cold, running water. Rap the
shells gently with a meat tenderizer
to crack them and remove the nuts
from the shells. Fold the nuts into
a clean tea towel and rub off the
papery skin.
MUSHIMONO - STEAMED

recipes.title: Layered Napa Cabbage With Green Beans 203 Mushimono - Steamed
recipes.transcription:
Preparation time: 45 minutes
Cooking
time : 25 minutes
Serves:
6
¾ - inch ( 2 cm) piece fresh ginger,
grated
I teaspoon fine sea salt
'I• teaspoon freshly ground
black pepper
2 tablespoons sake
IO oz (300 g) finely ground
(minced) chicken
12 large napa cabbage
( Chinese leaf) leaves
2 tablespoons
potato starch di ssolved
in 2 tablespoons water
I small carrot, scrubbed and
finely julienned
2 shiitake , stems discarded and caps
thinly sliced
8 thin green beans, topped
and julienned
r¼ cups (IO fl oz/300 ml) Katsuobushi
Dashi
(page 156)
2 tablespoons soy sauce
• I tablespoon sake
• I tablespoon mirin
LAYERED NAPA CABBAGE
WITH GREEN BEANS
The green beans in this dish give
color and texture, and the generous
portions make it a good candidate
for a one-dish supper.
Squeeze the juice from the grated
ginger into a bowl. Stir in the salt,
pepper, and sake. In a bowl, knead
the ginger juice mixture into the
chicken with your hands until well
incorporated.
Bring a large pot of salted water
to a boil. Rap the stem ends of the
cabbage leaves with a surigoki [wood en
pestle] or mallet to soften. Blanch
the leaves for 30 seconds in the
boiling water. Scoop out with a
wire-mesh sieve, shake off excess
water , and blot dry with clean tea
towels. Cut the leaves crosswise into
8-inch (20 cm) pieces and separate
into 3 piles.
Use the small extra
pieces for patching in here and
there on the middle layer, but save
the larg est pieces for the bottom
and top layers.
Measure out I tablespoon of the
potato starch slurry into a small
bowl and reserve for thickening the
dashi. Line the bottom o f an 8-inch
(20 cm) foil-lined square pan with
a removable bottom with an even
layer of one-third of the leaves.
Brush with some of the potato starch
slurry. Spread half of the chicken
mixture across the cabbage and top
with another layer of cabbage. Brush
again with the potato starch slurry,
spread in the rest of the chicken,
and top with a last layer of cabbage.
Brush with potato starch. Cover
tightly with foil.
Line a steamer basket with
cheesecloth (to make it eas ier
to remove the pan). Set up the
steamer and bring the water to
a boil. Place the pan in the
steamer basket, cover, and steam
for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile , in a saucepan, combine
the carrot , shiitake, green beans ,
dashi, soy sauce, sake, and mirin
and bring to a simmer. Stir in
the reserved I tablespoon potato
starch slurry and simmer gently
until glistening and ever so slightly
thickened , another 2-3 minutes.
Cut into 6 portions, spoon the silky
vegetable sauce over the layered
cabbage, and serve.

recipes.title: Layered Napa Cabbage Mushimono - Steamed
recipes.transcription:
Preparation time: 25 minutes
Cooking
time: 30 minutes

12 large
napa cabbage
( Chinese leaf) leaves

(minced)
pork

usukuchi shoyu

Japanese

LAYERED NAPA CABBAGE
Individual stuffed cabbage rolls are
a bit labor intensive , but you can
save time by deconstructing the
rolls: Just layer the steamed cabbage
leaves with the meat and get the
same tasty combination of flavors
and textures.
Set up a bamboo steamer in a
pan and bring the water to a boil.
Divide the napa cabbage ( Chinese
leaf) leaves into two piles , side by
side, in the steamer basket, cover,
and steam for 3 minutes. Flip
the leaves and steam for 3 more
minutes. Remove from the heat
and lay the leaves out side by side
on clean tea towels to cool. Pat
dry. (Keep the steamer ready for
steaming the rest of the dish.)
In a bowl, mix together the meat,
I tablespoon of the usukuchi sh'!J'u,
and the salt with a pair of saibashi
[cooking chopsticks) until the
ingredients are well incorporated.
In one bowl , whisk together 3 of
the
eggs. In a separate bowl, whisk
the remaining egg.
Line an 8-inch (20 cm) foil-
lined square pan with a removable
bottom with 4 of
the cabbage leaves ,
making sure to cover the complete
area , coming up the sides of the
pan slightly , and evenly distributing
the stem and leaf parts so the thick
stems are not all in one area. Cover
the cabbage leaves with half of
the meat mixture, top with the 3
whisked
eggs and another layer of
4 cabbage
leaves . Repeat with the
remaining meat , the last layer of
cabbage , and the last whisked egg
to provide a glossy surface to the
cooked dish.
Cover tightly with foil. Set in
the steamer , cover , and steam for
QO minutes.
Meanwhile , in a medium saucepan,
heat the chicken broth, remaining
I tablespoon usukuchi sh'!J'u, and the
mirin over medium-high heat. Stir
the potato starch mixture into the
broth and simmer for 2-3 minutes
to
thicken.
After steaming, let the cabbage rest
for 5 minutes before unmolding.
Cut into 6 portions and place each
in a shallow bowl. Nap with the hot ,
silky chicken broth .

recipes.title: Silky Napa Cabbage Layered With Ground Meat 205 Mushimono
recipes.transcription:

Cooking time, 35
minutes

napa cabbage

I ½ teaspoons flaky sea salt

• I medium carrot , scrubbed and

4 medium

(page 156)
SILKY NAPA CABBAGE
LAYERED WITH GROUND MEAT
This version of layered napa
cabbage ( Chinese leaf) contains
appreciably
more meat than the
other versions.
Set up a steamer in a pan and bring
the water to a boil. Stack the napa
cabbage ( Chinese leaf) leaves
in the
steamer basket , cover, and steam
until the stem ends have softened ,
5-7 minutes.
Lay the leaves out ,
sid e by side on a large baking sheet,
and sprinkle with ½ teasp o on of
the salt. (Keep the steamer ready
for steaming the rest of the dish.)
In large bowl, combine the onion,
carrot , shiitake, pork , and beef.
Break the eggs into the bowl and
add the panko, remaining
I teaspoon salt, and the pepper.
Mix the ingredients together using
a cutting motion with your flat
hand to avoid overworking the
meat. Stir in the milk to lighten
the mixture.
Line an 8-inch (20 cm) round
mold with 3 of
the cabbage
leaves-let the leaves come up the
sides of the pan a little. Sprinkle
evenly with I teaspoon of the
potato starch. Smooth half of the
meat mixture over the leaves , lay
another 3 cabbage leaves over the
meat, sprinkle with I teaspoon of
the potato starch, and spread the
second half of the meat over the
leaves. Spr inkle with I teaspoon
of the potato starch and lay the
remaining 3 leaves across the meat.
Tuck any errant leaves back inside
the pan. Cover tightly with foil.
Place the pan in the steamer. cover,
and steam until the meat has set ,
about 30 minutes.
In a small saucepan , dissolve
the remaining ½ tablespoon
potato starch in I tablespoon cold
water . Tip the juices that have
accumulated from the meat and
cabbage out of the pan and whisk
into the potato starch mixture
with the dashi. Simmer until
thickened and syrupy , but still
a silky, smooth sauce .
Let the layered cabbage sit for
IO minutes before unmolding
onto a large dinner plate. Cut
into wedges and serve napped with
the sauce.

STIR-FRIED VEGETABLES
WITH BURDOCK
Cobo [burdock root] is ubiquitous
in traditionaljapanese cooking.
Beside soups and simmered dishes,
burdock is frequently stir-fried
with carrots and seasoned with
soy sauce for
kinpira. Here, green
vegetables and seaweed elevate the
traditionalgobo-carrot kinpira.
Cut the komatsuna crosswise into
r½ inches (4 cm) wide pieces .
Drain the hijiki and cut it crosswise
into r½-inch (4 cm) pieces.
In a large frying pan, heat the
sesame oil over medium heat.
Scrape in the
gobo and chiles and
stir-fry until half cooked, but
fragrant, 2-3 minutes . Splash
in
the dashi, soy sauce , and mirin. Raise
the heat to high, stir to distribute
and cook for
I minute, stirring .
Reduce the heat to medium-low,
add the carrots, toss once or twice,
and stir-fry for 2 minutes . Once
the
pan liquid is bubbling, throw
in the hijiki, m'?Yashi, and komatsuna,
raise the heat to high, and cook for
I more minute.
When the greens have wilted and
are cooked through, sprinkle in the
black sesame seeds and spoon into
a pretty serving bowl. Serve hot or
at room temperature.
STIR-FRIED BURDOCK
WITH TOFU
Use top-quality tofu for this dish as
it will make a difference.
Set the tofu on a cutting board and
prop a small saucer underneath to
angle the board into the kitchen
sink (to catch drips). Lay another
cutting board on top of the tofu to
press out moisture for 20 minutes .
Break the pressed tofu into rough
pieces and drop into a bowl.
With your nondominant hand ,
hold the burdock above another
bowl and use a sharp knife to shave
thin slices off the end of it as you
rotate it (sasagaki; see page 446), like
sharpening the end of a stick.
In a large frying pan, heat the
sesame oil over medium-high heat.
Toss the burdock slivers into the oil
and stir - fry for 3-5 minutes. Add
the dashi, soy sauce , and mirin and
bring to a simmer. Strew in the negi,
shiitake, and broken up tofu. Toss
until the burdock has softened but
still retains a slight crunch , about
5 minutes. Serve hot or at room
temperature.
[ variation]
To add protein and richness , swirl
3 beaten
eggs over the top of the
dish and cook until the egg s are just
set , but still partly runny.

recipes.transcription:

minutes salting time

SARDINES WITH
CARROT-TOMATO SAUCE
Italian in feel, this dish remains
Japanese in conception. It is
delicious with Japanese rice or
baguette toasts.
Slice the heads off of the sardines
and cut down the belly with a sharp
knife . Pull out the guts, vertebrae ,
and tail and discard. You will have
6 fillets. Rinse under cold running

dinner plate and, holding your
hand 12 inches
(30 cm) above the
fish (to
ensure a light even coating) ,
salt on all sides with the salt. Let
sit for 30 minutes, refrigerated.
Heat a large, heavy frying pan over
Add the onion, piman, tomatoes,
carrot, and garlic to the pan and
cook, stirring, over medium-low
heat for about 3 minutes. Stir the
chicken stock into the vegetables,
bring the liquid to a quick boil,
adjust the heat to medium-high to
maintain a lively simmer, and cook
until the carrot s are soft and the

5 minutes .
Spoon the carrot-tomato sauce on
top of each sauteed sardine, squeeze

or at room temperature.
medium heat and drop in the butter @ p.2II
when you can feel the heat rising

STIR-FRIED EGGPLANT WITH
GINGER AND SESAME
Eggplant (aubergine) has a long
history of being paired with ginger.
The addition of sesame in the sweet
and salty sauce makes for a more
deeply flavored dish.
In a small, dry frying pan , toast the
sesame seeds until fragrant. Drop
into a suribachi [grinding bowl) and
smash slightly. In a small bowl,
whisk together the sesame, ginger ,
soy sauce , and mirin to make a sauce.
Slice the eggplants crosswise into
%-inc h (1
cm) rounds . In a large
frying pan, heat the sesame oil over
medium heat. Slide in the eggplant
pieces and negi, cover, and cook
over low heat , turning occasionally,
until the eggplant is cooked
through and ha s golden brown
spots, 5-7 minutes . Pour the sauce
over the hot eggplant and serve
right away or at room temperature.

STIR-FRIED SPINACH

This eye-catching dish-brown
mushrooms , brilliant green

yellow egg curds-makes a b eautifu l
side dish or one-dish meal.
In a large frying pan , melt the
butter over medium heat. Add all

they start giving off some liquid ,

the salt and pepper and strew in
the carrot and spinach. Continue

egg , wet your hand with cold

STIR-FRIED OKARA
AND VEGETABLES
The addition of okara [soybean
pulp] to this classic kinpira (vegetable
stir-fry flavored with soy sauce)
makes this a healthy and delicious
dish.
In a large dry wok , roast the okara

With your nondominant hand,
hold the burdock above a cutting

STIR-FRIED KABOCHA
Gently caramelized fried kabocha
(Japanese pumpkin) slices, flavored
with soy sauce and mirin, add a
welcome balance to any casual
Japanese meal.
Cut the kabocha slices crosswise
into pieces I¼ inches (3 cm) wide.
Heat a large enough frying pan
to hold the kabocha in one layer,
over medium heat. When you can
feel the heat coming off the pan ,
swirl in the sesame oil. Set the
kabocha in the frying pan in one
layer and sear for I minute or two
on each side until golden. Add I
tablespoon water, the soy sauce,
mirin, and sesame seeds. Cover , turn
the pieces occasionally, and cook
over low heat until the kabocha has
cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Toss with the salt and serve hot or
at room temperature.
STIR-FRIED LOTUS ROOT
Lotus root has a natural crunch
that makes it a good candidate
for stir-frying, since it retains
its appealing texture even after
cooking over high heat. Finishing
this dish with a creamy ,
dashi­
infused paste of black sesame seeds
makes for a pretty presentation .
Slide the warmed sesame seeds
into a
suribachi [grinding bowl] or
spice / nut grinder and process until
broken down, but not paste-like.
Slice the lotus root crosswise
into %-inch (! cm) rounds ,
half-rounds, or quarter-rounds,
depending on the diameter of the
lotus root.
In a large frying pan or wok , heat
the sesame oil over medium-high
heat until shimmering. Add the
lotus root and toss with two flat
wooden spoons until the roots are
glossy and starting to color , about
3 minutes.
Add the dashi, soy sauce ,
and mirin. Cover and simmer,
swirling occasionally, for 2 minutes
over
low heat. Pick the lotus root
pieces out with a pair of tongs and
drop into a medium serving bowl.
Stir the simmering liquids into the
ground sesame seeds to make a
loose paste. Fold the paste into the
lotus root and serve warm or at
room temperature.

MISO-INFUSED MEAT
AND VEGETABLES
Naturally just a bit sweet, the
combination of ingredients make
this a lovely dish of miso-infused
ground meat. Serve spooned over
white rice, tofu, cooked noodles,
or toast.
In a large frying pan , heat the oil
over medium heat. Add the onion
and saute gently
until softened
and translucent, about 2 minutes .
Add the ground (minced) meat

until the meat is half cooked, about
2 minutes.
Slide the carrot, piman,
and shiitake into the meat mixture
and continue stirring over medium

are cooked through, 5-7 minutes .
In

miso, dashi, and mirin. Fold into the

longer. It holds up well

SAUTEED VEGETABLES WITH
CHICKEN LIVER AND TOFU
The chicken liver adds flavor to this
vegetable stir-fry, while the tofu
introduces a mild creamy texture.
And the technique of using salted
rice bran to soften the intense liver

four whole garlic chives and not
just four garlic chive leaves.
Set the tofu on a cutting board and
prop a small saucer underneath it
to angle the board into the kitchen

cutting board on top of the tofu to
press out moisture for 20 minutes
before cutting into % - inch

the salted bran , taking care not to

medium bowl with cold water and

to rinse off the bran . Pat dry in a
clean tea towel.

I ½-inch (4 cm) lengths. Slice those

(2 cm)

(r cm) wide.

over medium heat until it starts to

sesame oiC soy sauce , and mirin. Add
the carrot, bok choy , piman, m~ashi,
and garlic chives
and stir-fry over
high heat until the vegetables are
cooked, 2- 3 minutes.
Serve hot.

miso and mirin. Scrape over the
vegetables and toss off heat until

temperature . Leftovers are fine
reheated or cold .
GREEN PEPPER KINPIRA
Kinpira-sauteed vegetables flavored
with soy sauce-are commonly cut
into julienne strips, and take some
time to prep. Here the piman are
quartered , making this dish a bit
quicker to prepare.
In a large frying pan , heat the
oil over medium heat until
shimmering but not smoking.
Throw in the piman and sear,
covered, for I minute on each side,
until the piman are crisp-tender
and browned in spots. Add the soy
sauce and mirin , stir - fry for another
minute to evaporate the liquid, and
slide the piman into a medium bowl.
Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and
serve hot.

This is one version of the

recipes.transcription:

Cooking time: 15 minutes
Serves: 6
3 cups (7 oz/200 g) moyashi [mung
bean sprouts]

• 3 ½ oz (JOO g) finely sliced
pork shou lder

• ¼ teaspoon fine sea salt

• ½ tablespoon soy sauce
SILKY BEAN SPROUTS
The pork shoulder in this dish
serves only to provide a bit of
richness, so there is just a sma ll
amount.
In small pot of boiling water,
blanch the m'!Yashi for 30 seconds.
Scoop out with a wire-mesh sieve
and drain.
In a large frying pan , heat the
oil over medium heat until
shimmering. Slide in the pork,
shiitake, carrot , celery , celery leaves ,
ginger , and m'!Yashi. Stir-fry until
the pork and vegetables are cooked
through, 5-7 minutes.
Sprinkle in
the salt.
In a sma ll saucepan, warm the
chicken stock. Whisk the potato
starch mixture slowly into the hot
chicken stock with the soy sauce.
Simmer gently until the mixture
reaches a silky , creamy texture ,
3- 5 minutes . Pour the sauce over
the pork and vegetables and serve.
ROLLED SPINACH OMELET
Simple in execution but pretty
in presentation, and delicious as
well, these little rolled omelets are
useful to put in your repertoire.
Other leafy greens can be easily
substit uted . Serve as a bite before
dinner, or as a side dish.
Bring a pot of water to a boil.
Hold the spinach stem ends in the
boiling water for 30 secon ds, then
submerge the leave s in the water
and cook for 30 more seconds .
Scoop out with a wire-mesh sieve
and cool under running water.
Align by stem ends and squeeze
down the length of the leav es to
remove excess water.
Break each egg into a sma ll bowl
and whisk in 1/a teaspoon salt into
each. Heat a rectangular Japanese
omelet pan (page 445) over
medium-low h eat until you can feel
the heat rise up , and measure in
¾ teaspoon of the oil. Tilt the pan
to spread the oil across and scrape
in the egg from one of the bowls.
Roll across the surface of the pan
and cook for I minute or so, until
the egg has set but still shiny . Turn
the egg omelet out of the pan onto
a cutting board and repeat with the
remaining oil and egg mixture.
Turn the second omelet out onto
the cutting board next to the first.
Flip the omelets, so the shiny side
is up . Divide the spinach in half
and form each half into a log that is
as long as the omelet is wide. Place
a log at the bottom end of each
omelet, making sure that the end
of the spinach log comes right to
the outer edges. Roll up tightly and
cut in half at a diagonal. Stand up
and drizzle a heaping ¼ teaspoon
soy sauce over the spinach in each
omelet.

This is a classic dish that normally

In a bowl , mix together the eggs,

layer of the egg mixture , tilting the
pan to evenly cover the bottom of
EGG THREADS
Use these egg threads as a topping
in sushi dishes, donburi [rice bowls],
or salads.
Break the egg into a small bowl
and beat with a fork to emulsify,
but do not create a froth. Add the

Spread the oil with a spatula. Swirl

the pan, but not go up the sides.

JAPANESE-STYLE
SCRAMBLED EGGS
Scrambled eggs flavored with soy
sauce and katsuobushi make a brilliant
lunch , especially when served
with quickJapanese pickles or a
vegetable dish and rice .
In a bowl , whisk together the eggs,
usukuchi sh'!)'u, min·n, and salt. In a

resistant spatula , draw the egg

side and tilt the pan against the

STIR-FRIED EGG WITH BEEF
Egg and meat stir-fries are one
of the quickest , mo st convenient
dinners , and only need something
green to make them a complete
one-dish meal.
In a pot of salted boiling water,

I minute . Scoop out with a wire­

Break the eggs into a medium bowl

The success of this dish hinges on

In a large heavy frying pan,
heat the canola (rapeseed) oil

Negi (Japanese leek] and chicken is
a classic yakitori combination , but

In a small bowl, toss the chicken

SPICY FRIED CHICKEN
MEATBALLS
Serve these spicy little meatballs as
savory bites to accompany drinks
before dinner.
Place the chicken in a bowl. Sift
the flour over the chicken and mix
in with a pair of saibashi [cooking
chopsticks]. Fold in the egg, soy
sauce , mirin, negi, carrot, shiitake,
and ichimi togarashi until all of the
ingredients are well incorporated.
Using two soup spoons, form
12 small balls about the size of large
walnuts.
Pour 3 1/+ inches ( 8 cm) oil into a
heavy medium pot and heat over
medium-high heat until hot but
not smoking. Working in batches,
fry the meatballs until golden
brown and the bubbles sputtering
out from the surfaces have
subsided, about 5 minutes. Drain
on
absorbent paper towels. Serve
the batches hot as they come out of
the fryer.
Serve hot with a cocktail pick stuck
in each one to avoid burned fingers
and a small saucer of soy sauce or
por,zu, for dipping .
DEEP-FRIED CHICKEN NUGGETS
Fried chicken nuggets, often
purchased on the fly at convenience
stores, are one of the best-loved
foods of Japanese youth. Making
them at home does take a bit of
time , but cutting the chicken into
smaller pieces makes the frying
go faster.
Drop the chicken into a gallon­
size resealable plastic bag. Add the
soy sauce, mirin, ginger , and ichimi
togarashi and massage to distribute.
Marinate for at least 30 minute s.
Pour 3 1/+ inches (8 cm) oil into
a heavy medium pot and heat
over medium heat. Remove
about 12 pieces of chicken from
th e marinade and shake excess
marinade off. Dredge in the potato
starch. Fry until golden brown
and the extruding bubbles have
subsided , 3- 5 minutes . Drain
on
absorbent paper towels . Repeat with
the remaining chicken. Serv e the
bat ches hot as they come out of
th e fryer.

recipes.transcription:

4-inch (ro cm) piece naga imo
[mountain yam] , peeled

DEEP-FRIED DAIKON WITH
BLACK SESAME
Daikon dipped in grated naga imo
[mountain yam] before frying is
crispy and juicy. These are best
hot , though are still tasty at room
temperature.
Grate the naga imo on an oroshigane
U apanese grating plate] into a
viscous mass . Measure the flour into
a medium bowl and slowly whisk
in % cup (5 fl oz/r50 ml) water to
make a smooth batter. Stir in the
naga imo and black sesame seeds.

¾ - inch (2 cm) rounds , then into
half - moons or quarter-moons.
Fold the daikon pieces into the bowl
of batter with a rubber spatula to
coat on all sides.
Add the sesame oil to a heavy
medium pot and pour in canola
(rapeseed) oil to come up
3
1/+ inches (8 cm) up. Heat over
medium-high heat until hot but
not smoking. Working in batches
(do not crowd the pot) , fry the

FRIED DRIED PERSIMMONS
Hoshigaki [dried persimmons]
are available from late October
through December inJapan. Since
they are semi-dried, the only way
to extend their shelf life is to freeze
them. Hopefully, you can find
some , since they are delicious. Eat
these fried persimmons hot with a
glass of frothy beer or champagne .
In a small saucepan of boiling water ,
cook the quail eggs for 3 minutes .
Cool under cold running water
and peel.
Make a vertical slit in the side of
each hoshigaki and pry out the pits

the hoshigaki gap by threading a
toothpick diagonally through the
bottom third to the top third of

starch and fine sea
salt into a bowl
big enough to hold one hoshigaki
and thin with 2 tablespoons cold
water. Roll each hoshigaki in the
potato starch liquid to cover and
fry until crisp and golden , with
the dried hoshigaki starting to show
through the white starch coating ,
and the lively bubbles beginning to
subside , about 5 minutes. Drain
on absorbent paper towels for l-2
seconds, remove the toothpick, and
slice in half crosswise . Serve hot,
taking care to avoid the tough calyx
(cap) at the stem end. Sprinkle the
yolks with a tiny pinch of the flaky
sea salt, if you think they need it.

A cult favorite of foreigners and

of the potato starch over the tofu
and nudge the pieces around gently
to coat evenly with starch.
Heat 3
'/• inches
(8 cm) oil in a
heavy medium pot over high heat
until hot but not smoking. Shake
off excess starch. Working in
batches (do not crowd the pot) ,
drop the tofu into the oil and fry
until golden brown, 30 seconds.
Drain on absorbent paper towels.
Place the
konbu on the bottom of
a heavy medium pot. Add 2 cups
(16
fl oz/500 mi) water,
the soy
sauce , mirin, sake, and salt . Bring
to a lively simmer over medium­
high heat and cook for 3 minutes .
Carefully nestle the fried tofu in
the broth, top with the daikon, and
gently simmer until the daikon has
absorbed flavor , 3 minutes.
Place
two pieces of tofu each on 6
deep-sided saucers, ladle the daikon­
dashi over, and serve hot.

MONO - FRIED

recipes.title: Dashi-Simmered Deep-Fried Ganmodoki 234 Agemono
recipes.transcription:
Preparation time: I hour
Cooking time: 20 minutes
Makes: 12
For
the croquettes:
I (ro'/2 oz/300 g) momendofu or
Japanese-style soft block tofu
I heaping tablespoon dried hijiki
2 small dried
shiitake, soaked in boiling
water for 30 minutes
• I tablespoon mirin
• I tablespoon sake
½ teaspoon fine sea salt
1/2 medium carrot, scrubbed and
finely chopped
2 oz
(60 g) gobo [burdock], scrubbed
and finely chopped
I teaspoon black sesame seeds, warmed
in a small, dry frying pan
2 tablespoons
potato starch
Neutral oil, such as canola (rapeseed) ,
peanut, or safflower , for deep-frying
• Boiling water
For the dashi :
2½ cups (20 fl oz / 600 ml)
Katsuobushi
Dashi (page 156)
3 tablespoons
usukuchi shoyu
· 2 tablespoons
sake
• 2 tablespoons
mirin
DASHI-SIMMERED DEEP-FRIED
GANMODOKI
These homemade ganmodoki (tofu
croquettes) are also tasty on their
own. Instead of simmering them
in dashi, you could alternatively
serve the croquettes drizzled with
soy sauce and garnished with grated
ginger, chopped scallions (spring
onion) , and shaved katsuobushi,
Make the croquettes: Set the tofu
on a cutting board and prop a
small saucer underneath to angle
the board into the kitchen sink
(to catch drips), Lay another cutting
board on top of the tofu to press
out moisture for 20 minutes.
Place the hijiki in a large bowl
in the kitchen sink and fill with
water . Soak for IO minutes, drain,
fill again , and soak for IO more
minutes . Drain and pat the hijiki
dry in a clean tea towel. Finely
chop. Drain the shiitake and discard
the stems. Blot the caps dry and
finely chop .
Squeeze
the tofu one last time and
drop into a suribachi [grinding bowl]
or large mortar. Mash in the mirin,
sake, and salt until well emulsified
and fluffy . Fold the hijiki, shiitake,
carrot, gobo, black sesame seeds,
and potato starch into the tofu
mixture and beat with a wooden
spoon until evenly incorporated.
Pat out into 12 small plump
round
croquettes and place on a piece of
parchment paper .
In a heavy medium pot, heat
4 inches (ro cm) of oil over
medium heat until hot but not
smoking. Working in two batches ,
fry the croquettes until golden
brown , 3-5 minutes. Drain on
absorbent paper towels.
Place the fried croquettes in a large
wire-mesh sieve and pour a steady
stream of boiling water over them
for IO seconds to remove oil.
Make the dashi: In a medium
saucepan , bring the dashi to a
simmer over medium-high heat.
Stir in the usukuchi sh'!)'u, sake, and
mirin. Slip in the croquettes and
simmer gently , but not sluggishly,
for 3-5 minutes to absorb the
simmering liquids .

recipes.title: Fried Kabocha Balls 235 Agemono
recipes.transcription:
Preparation time, I hour
Cooking time, 45 minutes
Makes, II!
5 ¼ oz (150 g) momendofu or
Japanese - style soft block tofu
10½ oz (300 g) lightly peeled and
seeded kabocha (Japanese pumpkin)
• I teaspoon fine sea salt
• I sma ll carrot , scrubbed and diced
½ cup (55 g) walnuts , coarsely chopped
· IO½ oz (300 g) naga imo
[mountain yam)
3 ½ oz (100 g) so men noodles
(2 tab-enclosed
bunches) ,
broken into eighths
Neutral oil , such as canola (rapeseed),
peanut, or safflower, for deep-frying
• ½ teaspoon flaky sea salt
FRIED KABOCHA
BALLS
The se little kabocha-tofu ball s
are a bit of work to prepare , but
are well worth the effort, as they
are spectacular with drink s before
dinner. Contact with the flesh of
naga imo [mountain yam] causes an
itchy reaction, so it is best to use
rubber gloves when grating it.
Set the tofu on a cutting board and
prop a small saucer underneath to
angle the board in to the kitchen
sink (to catch drips). Lay another
cutting board on top of the tofu to
press out moisture for ~O minutes.
Set up a steamer and bring the
water to a boil.
Rub the kabocha (Japanese
pumpkin) with the fine sea
salt.
Place in the steamer basket , cover ,
and stea m until soft , abo ut 25
minutes.
Transfer to a bowl and
smash the flesh. Mash the tofu int o
the kabocha. Fold in the carrot and
walnuts and, using two soup spoons,
form into golf ball-sized spheres.
Put the balls on a baking sheet.
Grate the noga imo to a viscous mas s
on an oroshigane U apanese grating
plate) and scrape into a soup bowl,
and set that to the immediate
right of the baking sheet with the
kabocha-tofu balls. Scatter the cut
somen noodles onto a large dinner
plate and break up the noodles
just a bit more. Position that plate
next to the yam bowl. Place an
empty baking sheet next to the somen
plate. Pick up a glob of naga imo and
stretc h it out on your left hand.
Set a kabocha ball on top of the
yam and smooth the yam around
the ball. Drop the ball on the plate
of cut somen, then using your clean
(dry) right hand , roll it in the somen
noodles by nudging it with your
hand. Once covered in noodles,
arrange on the clean baking sheet.
Pour 3¼ inches (8 cm) neutral
oil into a heavy medium pot and
heat until hot but not smoking.
Working in batches (do not crowd
the pot), fry the kabocha balls
until deeply golden brown , about
3 minutes.
Drain on absorbent
paper towels. Serve immediately
with flaky sea salt mounted in
a small pile on the plate.
235 AGEMONO
- FRIED

recipes.title: Summer Vegetable Tempura Fried Eggplant With Sour Plum
recipes.transcription:
Preparation time: 30 minu tes
Cooking time: 20 minutes
Serves:
6
Neutral oil, such as canola (rapeseed) ,
peanut, or safflower, for deep-frying
ro½ oz (300 g)Japanese eggplant
(aubergines)
l cup (5 1/• oz/!50 g) unbleached
cake flour
l pinch of fme sea salt
l cup (8 fl oz/250 ml) cold
sparkling water
I (5 1/• oz/!50 g) unpeeled red potato,
scrubbed and
cut crosswise into ¼-inch
( 6 mm) slices
• 9 oz
(250 g) lightly peeled and seeded
kabocha (Japanese pumpkin), cut into
wedges ½ inch (12 mm) thick
• 18 thin green beans
(4 1/2 oz/!25 g), topped
• 6 green shiso leaves
• Tempura Dipping Broth (page 157),
for serving
Preparation time: IO minutes
Cooking time: IO minutes
Serves: 6
6 medium Japanese eggplants
(aubergines), I lb 2 oz (500 g), stem
ends trimmed
Neutral oil, such as canola (rapeseed) ,
peanut, or safflower, for deep-frying
4 umeboshi
[salted sour plum]. pitted
and
finely chopped
½ tablespoon soy sauce
• I tablespoon mirin
I package (3 oz/85 g) daikon sprouts,
cut off their sponge base
SUMMER VEGETABLE TEMPURA
Almost any vegetable can be cut up
and fried as tempura. The key is
an extremely light , eggless batter
that relies on cold sparkling water
and some ice to keep it effervescent
and cool.
Pour 6 inches (15 cm) oil into
a heavy medium pot and set over
low heat.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the
eggplants (aubergines) lengthwise
from the bottom up to the calyx
(cap) area, making sure to leave
the calyx intact. Fan the slices out
a little.
In a medium bowl, whisk together
the flour and fine salt. Slowly whisk
in the sparkling water.
Increase the heat under the oil
to medium and bring the oil to
340-350°F (170-180°C). Working
in batches, dip each vegetable type
into the batter, shake off drips,
and gently slip in the oil. (Fry
the green beans in clumps of
3 .) Fry , turning with chopsticks ,
until the bubbling quiets down
and the vegetables are golden
brown ,
1-2 minutes , depending
on size. Fry
the shiso leaves last , for
15 seconds or so, as they brown
quickly. Drain on absorbent paper
towels. Eat hot , dipped in small
bowls of the tempura dipping broth.
[variation]
If you prefer egg in your tempura
batter , whisk l beaten egg (2 oz/55 g)
into the batter.
[QJ p.239
FRIED EGGPLANT WITH
SOUR PLUM
Here , the puckery sour plum offsets
the creamy richness of the fried
eggplant (aubergine).
Slice the eggplants (aubergines)
diagonally into thick triangular
chunks (rangiri; see
page 446).
Pour 3¼ inches (8 cm) neutral oil
into a heavy medium pot and heat
over medium-high heat until hot
but not smoking . Slip about half
of the eggplant pieces into the
hot oil and fry until golden brown
and the bubbling has subsided,
2-3 minutes.
Drain on absorbent
paper towels. Wait I minute for the
oil to reheat, fry the other eggplant
slices, and drain.
In a medium bowl , thin the
chopped umeboshi with the soy
sauce and mirin. Once the fried
eggplant slices have cooled to room
temperature, add them to the
umeboshi mixture and toss .
Scatt er a large dinner plate or
platter with the daikon sprouts and
mound the eggplant attractive ly on
top of the sprouts.
[variation]
Omit the daikon sprouts and add
l cup (8 fl oz/250 mi) grated daikon
to the umeboshi mixture before
tossing with the eggplant.
AGEMONO - FRIED

recipes.title: Deep-Fried Eggplant In Dashi Eggplant Fritters
recipes.transcription:
Preparation time, 25 minutes
Cooking time: IO minutes
Serves, 6
• 6 med iumjapane se eggplants
(aub ergines) (r lb 2 oz / 500 g) , calyxes
(caps) intact
• I tablespoon fine sea salt
• 2½ cups (20 fl oz / 600 mi)
Katsu o bushi
Dashi (page 156)
• 2 tablespoons soy sauc e
• I tablespoon mirin
• Neutral oil, such as canola (rapeseed),
peanut , or safflower , for deep-frying
• I tablespoon finely slivered fresh ginger
Preparation time, r5 minutes
Cooking time , r5 minutes
Serves, 6
I lb 2 oz (500 g) J apane se eggplants
(aubergines) , stems ends trimmed
• 'I• teaspoon fine sea salt
Neutral oil , such as canola (rapeseed) ,
peanut , or safflower , for deep-frying
½ cup (75 g) unbleached all-purpose
(plain) flour
½ cup (4 fl oz/r25 m l) whole milk
I egg, at room temperature , separated
2 tablespoons black sesame seeds or
coarsely chopped parsley
• 1/ 2 tea spoon flaky s e a salt
DEEP-FRIED EGGPLANT
IN DASHI
Finishing the eggplant in dashi
lightens the dish.
Slice a thin lengthwise portion
of the skin off o f each side o f the
eggplant (aubergine), and cut
lengthwise into 4-6 slices
about
% inch (r cm) thick. Soak in a bowl
with 2½ cup s (20 fl oz/600 mi)
water
and the salt for IO minutes.
Drain the eggplant , lay out acro ss a
clean tea towel, and pat dry .
In a medium saucepan , bring
the dashi, soy sauce , and mirin to
a simmer. Remove immediately
from the heat and transfer to a
rectangular refrigerator container
(big enough to hold the eggplant)
to cool.
Pour 3' /• inches
(8 cm) of oil into
a heavy medium pot and heat over
medium heat to 340-350°F (r70-
r800C). Working in batches , fry the
eggplant until lightly golden . Drain
on absorbent paper towels . Slip the
hot fried eggplant into the dashi and
refrigerate to chill .
Serve chilled, garnished with ginger .
EGGPLANT FRITTERS
The batter protects the eggplant
from absorbing too much oil, and
the black sesame helps to create an
appealing light and crispy coating
on the eggplant pieces .
Halve the eggplants (aubergines)
lengthwise , then cut crosswise into
3-4 pieces. Sprinkle the cut sides
with 'I• teaspoon of the fine salt and
let sit for 5 minutes.
Wipe off the
salt and blot off any moisture with
a clean tea towel.
Pour 2 inches (5 cm) of oil into
a heavy medium pot and heat over
low heat.
Meanwhile , in a medium bowl ,
whisk together the flour and
remaining ½ teaspoon fine salt.
Whisk in the milk and egg yolk until
smooth. Stir in the black sesame
seeds (or chopped parsley) . In a
small bowl , beat the egg white until
stiff . Fold the egg white into the
batter , taking care not to smash
the whites.
In crease the heat to medium, and
once the oil is hot, fry th e eggplant
in batche s. Drop the eggplant
pieces into the batt er to coat. Slip
into the oil (do not crowd the
pot) and deep - fry until burnished
orangey-brown , about 2 minutes.
Drain on absorbent paper towels.
Line a dinner plate with a folded up
piece of
washi Uapanese calligraphy
paper] and arrange the eggplant
fritters on the plate . Place the flaky
sea salt in a small mound on the
paper and serve the eggplant with
the salt right away while hot.

recipes.title: Lotus "Croquettes" Pickled Red Ginger Fritters 242 Agemono
recipes.transcription:
Preparation time: 55 minutes
Cooking time : 20 minutes
Serves, 6-8
IO ½ oz (300 g) lotus root, peeled
• 4 tablespoons
potato starch
• 3 tablespoons
barley miso
• 10½ oz (300 g) finely ground
(minced) pork
• ½ small onion, finely diced
• ½ small carrot, finely diced

(1'/• oz/35
g), finely diced
2 tablespoons
finely chopped curly or
Italian parsley

unbleached all-purpose
(plain) flour

g) julienned

LOTUS "CROQUETTES"
While not traditional croquettes,
the lotus slices inside the crispy
pork coating give a lovely crunch
to these fried rounds (or half
rounds). The meat coating on this
fried lotus gives the dish substance,
making it a good choice for a side
dish or a main course if served with
a salad .
Slice the lotus root crosswise into
'/•-inch (5
mm) rounds or half­
rounds, depending on the diameter
of the root. In a bowl, whisk I cup
(8 fl oz/250 ml) cold water into
2 tablespoons
of the potato starch.
Add the lotus root to the bowl and
soak for IO minutes to remove
bitterness.
In a bowl, mash the miso into the
pork until well emulsified. Fold
in the onion, carrot, piman, and
parsley.
Drain the lotus root and pat
dry on a clean tea towel. Dust
with the remaining 2 tablespoons
potato
starch and shake off the
excess. Smooth a thin coating
(1/ 1•-'/s-inch/2-3 mm) of
the meat mixture around the
lotus root. Arrange on a large
dinner plate.
Pour 3 'I• inches (8 cm) oil into a
heavy medium pot and heat over
medium-low heat.
In a small bowl, beat the eggs
and whisk with the flour to form
a loose paste . Pour the mixture
on top of the meat-coated lotus
root and flip to coat. Working in
batches (do not crowd the pot),
drop the croquettes into the oil
and fry until most of the bubbles
have subsided, about
3 minutes .
Adjust the
heat if browning too
quickly . Drain on absorbent paper
towels and serve hot.
PICKLED RED GINGER FRITTERS
Benishoga [pickled red ginger] often
contains red dye, so take care to
find a natural version such as
the one from Ohsawa (either the
threads or the fine slices
will work) .
These hot little fried morsels make
addictive bites before dinner,
especially when served with a beer .
Grate the nago imo to a viscous mass
on an oroshigane Uapanese grating
plate] and measure out
4 tablespoons.
Measure
the flour into a medium
bowl and stir in ½ cup (4 fl
oz/
125 ml) water , the grated nago imo,
and the salt to make a smoothly
sticky batter. Fold in the drained
benishoga.
Pour 3 '/• inches (8 cm) of the two
oils - in a proportion of 7 parts
canola
(rapeseed) oil to 3 parts
sesame oil-into
a heavy medium
pot and heat over medium-high
heat until hot but not smoking
(around 350°FII75°C) .
Working in batches, use two soup
spoons to dollop smallish amounts
of batter into the oil and fry until
golden brown and cooked through ,
3-5 minutes. Adjust the heat if
browning too quickly . Drain on
absorbent paper towels. Serve hot.

Kakiage is a type of tempura in which
the ingredients are chopped and

The center of the fritters should
be cooked, but remain just ever­
so-slightly spongy, which can be
tricky if they get too large. These

3'/• inches

FRIED MISO RICE BALLS
Though not commonly found in
modern-day Japan , these little
miso dango were once a convenient
way for farming families to use
up leftover rice and were served
as an afternoon snack or as part
of a bento box.
In a medium bowl, break the rice
up with large chopsticks and add

Moisten your palms with cold water

recipes.title: Sardines Fried With Pickled Red Ginger Curry-Seasoned
recipes.transcription:
Preparation time: 20 minutes
Cooking
time: 5 minutes
Serves: 6
6 fresh sardines (r'h lb/600 g)
• I tablespoon umesu [sour plum
"vinegar", page 442)
Neutral
oil , such as canola (rapeseed),
peanut, or safflower, for shallow-frying
1/, cup (1% oz/50 g) unbleached all­
purpose (plain) flour
2 eggs,
at room temperature
• r½ tablespoons finely chopped
benishoga
[pickled red ginger]
Preparation time: IO minutes
Cooking time: 5 minutes
Serves:
6
I whole mackerel (r1/, lb/600 g),
cleaned, filleted, pin bones removed
• ½ teaspoon flaky sea salt
• ½ teaspoon hot or mild curry powder
• I tablespoon unbleached all-purpose
(plain) flour
• Neutral oil , such as canola (rapeseed),
peanut, or safflower , for deep-frying
3 sudachi,
I yuzu , or ½ Meyer lemon,
for serving
SARDINES FRIED WITH
PICKLED RED GINGER
The brightness of the pickled
ginger makes these little fried
fish an
excellent choice as an
accompaniment to cocktails before
dinner. Look for a pickled red
ginger without red food dye (I like
Ohsawa). The umesu [sour plum
"vinegar"]-actually the brine from
salting sour plums-is also available
from Ohsawa .
Cut off the heads of the sardines
and make a slice down the belly
toward the tail with a sharp knife.
Pull out the guts, vertebrae, and
tail , to fillet. Also cut off the hard
fins on
the back of the sardines.
Rinse under cold running water
and blot dry. Lay the fish on
a
dinner plate and sprinkle with
the umesu.
Pour ½ inch (12 mm) oil into a
large heavy frying pan and heat over
low heat while you prepare the fish
for
frying.
Measure the flour into a flat­
bottomed medium bowl. Whisk
in the egg yolks and benishoga with
a fork . The batter will be fairly stiff .
Dip each fillet in
the batter until
lightly coated and set back down on
the plate .
Adjust the heat to medium and
once you can feel the heat rising
from the oil, slide each fillet into
the
oil , introducing each one gently
at the edge of the pan. Fry until
golden brown and the oil bubbles
have subsided, about 2 minutes
on
each side . Blot for I-2 minutes
on
absorbent paper towels. Serve hot.
CURRY-SEASONED
FRIED MACKEREL
While mackerel is commonly used in
Japan and Mediterranean countries,
it seems underappreciated in the
United States, though perhaps that
is changing. Mackerel is best in the
autumn when the meat has high
oil content.
Pat the fillets dry with absorbent
paper towels. Cut each fillet
crosswise
into thirds and sprinkle
on all sides with the salt. In a wide
shallow bowl, whisk together the
curry powder and flour and dredge
each fillet in
the curry flour to coat.
Shake off the excess and place on
a large dinner plate.
Pour 3 'I• inches (8 cm) neutral oil
into a heavy medium pot and heat
over medium-high heat until hot
but not smoking. Working in two
batches, fry the coated mackerel
until golden brown, I-2 minutes.
Drain on absorbent paper towels.
Serve on individual small plates
with half of a sudachi or a small
wedge ofyuzu.

recipes.title: Rice Croquettes Agemono - Fried
recipes.transcription:
Preparation time, I hour 30 minutes
Cooking time, 20 minutes
Makes, 12 croquettes
I cup (7 oz/200 g) uncooked
Japanese rice
1/+ cup (1½ oz/40 g) hikiwari mugi or
oshimugi [flattened barley]
Canola (rapeseed) oil, for frying
• I medium onion, diced
3½ oz (IOO g) ground (minced) pork
• 1¾ oz (50 g) ground (minced) beef
I medium carrot, scrubbed and diced
2 piman
or small green peppers,
(2½ oz/70 g), diced
8 large enoki mushrooms, diced
• I teaspoon flaky sea salt
½ teaspoon freshly ground
black pepper
7 oz (200 g) naga imo [mountain yam].
peeled and finely grated
1/+ cup (1 1/+ oz/35 g) unbleached all ­
purpose
(plain) flour
• I egg, beaten
I cup (2 ½ oz/75 g) panko
4 tablespoons
gold sesame oil
RICE CROQUETTES
A bit like aJapanese version
of Italian arancini (croquettes
made from leftover risotto), the
mountain yam acts as a binder and
the barley provides texture. These
croquettes make an excellent light
lunch, if served with vegetable side
dishes or a large salad . The meat
can be omitted for a vegetarian
version.
Wash and soak the rice (see
Japanese Rice, page 291). Stir in
the barley and cook, aerate , and
rest according to the directions
for Japanese Rice. Cool to room
temperature in a medium bowl,
about 30 minutes.
In a large frying pan , heat
½ tablespoon canola (rapeseed) oil
and heat over medium-low heat.
Add the onion and saute until
soft,
about 2 minutes.
Add the ground
meat and continue breaking up and
stir-frying until no longer pink,
1-2 minutes.
Stir in the carrot,
piman, and enoki. Season with the
salt and pepper and cook until the
carrots have softened, about
3 minutes.
Cool in a medium bowl
to room temperature.
Cut the cooled meat and vegetables
into the cooked rice with a rice
paddle or a wooden spoon. Fold
in the grated naga imo until well
incorporated and the mixture
forms a mass. Divide into
12 portions, pat each into an oval
patty , and set on a dinner plate.
Place the plate of patties in the
refrigerator, uncovered, for
30 minutes to chill.
Once chilled, set up 3 shallow
bowls. Put the flour in one, the
beaten egg in the second, and
the panko in the third. Dredge the
patties first in
the flour and shake
off the excess, then dip in the
beaten egg , and finally roll
in
the panko.
Pour 3 1/+ inches (8 cm) canola
(rapeseed) oil into a heavy medium
pot. Add the sesame oil. Heat over
medium heat until hot. Working
in batches (do not crowd the pot),
fry the croquettes until the lively
bubbling starts to subside and
the croquettes are deeply golden
brown, 2-3 minutes . (If browning
too fast , adjust the heat.) Drain on
absorbent paper towels. Serve hot.
AGEMONO - FRIED

recipes.title: Soybean Croquettes Salmon Croquettes 250 Agemono - Fried
recipes.transcription:
Preparation time, 35 minutes
Cooking time, 20 minute s
Makes,
6 croquettes
1½ cups (7oz/200 g) cooke d soybeans
(from ½ cup/roo g dried)
2 tablespoons
unbleached pastry flour
• 1½ teaspoon s flaky sea salt
• ½ teaspoon freshly ground
black pepper
½ small onion, finely chopped
½ small carrot, finely chopped
2 medium
shiitake , stems discarded
and caps finely chopped
4 tablespoons
coarsely chopped walnuts
7 oz (200 g) naga imo [mountain
yam]. peeled
½ cup plus 2 table spoo ns (1½
oz/
45 g)
panko
• Neutral oil, such as canola (rapeseed),
peanut, or safflower, for deep-frying
Preparation time, 50 minutes
Cooking time, 15 minutes
Makes, 12 small
croquettes
11/, lb (700 g) medium-large
potatoe s, peeled
l small carrot , scrubbed
• 1/2 tablespoon fine sea salt
5 tablespoons whole milk, heated
• 1/2 teaspoon flaky sea salt
• 'I• teaspoon freshly ground
black pepper
l can (6 oz/r70 g)
line-caught salmon,
dr ained and flaked
2 tablespoons
chopped scallion
(spring onion)
½ teaspoon grated fresh ginger
• ½ teaspoon ichimi togarashi
[powdered Japanese red chile]
l egg , at room temperature, whisked
• Neutral oil , such as canola (rapeseed),
peanut, or safflower, for deep-frying
• 4 tabl espoons potato starch
•
Ponzu, for serving
SOYBEAN CROQUETTES
Croquettes , commonly sold
in Japanese meat shops or
supermarkets , are often made
with potato, pumpkin, or even
creamed crab. Adding walnuts to
these vegetable-packed croquettes
enhances the slightly nutty flavor
of soybeans. When handling aga
imo [mountain yam] it is best to
wear rubber gloves, since contact
with the flesh causes temporary
itchiness.
In a medium bowl, smash the
cooked soybeans until they have
broken down, yet have not rea ched
a smooth paste. Mash in the flour,
l teaspoon of the salt, and the
pepper until well incorporated.
Mix in the onion, carrot, shiitake,
and walnuts. Grate the peeled
naga imo on an oroshigane U apanese
grating plate] to a viscous mass,
and stir half of the grated naga imo
into the soybean mixture. Divide
the mixture into sixths and form
spheres the size of golf balls . Set
on a large plate and scrape the
remaining half of the grated naga imo
over the balls, making su re all sides
are coated with yam. Roll each ball
in panko.
Pour 3 1/+ inches ( 8 cm) neutral oil
into a heavy medium pot and heat
over medium heat. Working in
batches , fry the croquettes slowly,
turning frequently to ensure even
coloring, until golden brown,
4-6 minutes.
Drain on absorbent
paper towels . Serve hot.
SALMON CROQUETTES
These spicy little patties are best hot
while the starch is still crispy. As
they cool, the coating will become
a bit chewy.
Halve the potatoes crosswise and
drop into a heavy medium saucepan
with the carrot. Cover two-thirds
of the way up with cold water, add
the fine sea sa lt , and bring to a boil
over high heat. When the carrot is
about half-cooked (3-5 minutes),
remove from the boiling water and,
when cool enough to handle , cut
into ¼-inch (6 mm) dice. Cook
the potatoes until they are soft in
the center, for a total of 8 minutes .
Drain and mash the potatoes with
a potato ricer or sturdy fork with
large tines. Smash in the heated
milk , flaky salt , and pepper .
In a small bowl, toss the salmon
with the scallion (spring onion),
ginger, and ichimi togarashi. Fold this
mixture into the mashed potatoes
along with the diced carrots and
whisked egg. Form into 12 small
plump
patties. Refrigerate for
30 minutes. (You can form the
croquettes ahead to this point and
refrigerate if you only want to fry a
few at a time. They will hold up well
for l-2 days.)
Pour 3 1/+ inches (8 cm) of oil into
a heavy medium pot and heat over
medium heat. Roll the croquettes
in the potato starch. Working in
batches, fry until golden brown,
3-5 minutes. Drain on absorbent
paper towels.
Serve the croquettes burning hot
with po= for dipping .
250 AGEMONO - FRIED

recipes.title: Pan-Fried Fish Balls Fried Chicken Meatballs With Nori
recipes.transcription:
Preparation time: 25 minutes
Cooking time: 15 minutes
Makes: 12 fish balls
1% lb (720 g) fresh sardines , skinned
and filleted (bones reserved)
• 4 small
or 2 large shiso leaves ,
finely chopped
• l tablespoon finely chopped
fresh
ginger
l tablespoon finely chopped scallion
(spring onion)
l tablespoon black sesame seeds ,
warmed slightly in a dry, small frying pan
• 2 tablespoons brown rice miso
2 tablespoons
unbleached pastry flour ,
plus more for dusting
4 tablespoons
canola (rapeseed) oil
Preparation time: 15 minutes
Cooking time: IO minutes
Makes: 24 meatballs
½ tablespoon fine sea salt
• l small carrot , scrubbed
I lb 2 oz (500 g) finely ground
(minced) chicken
4 shiitake , stems
discarded and caps
finely chopped
l medium negi or 3 fat scallions
(spring onions), finely chopped
• l egg , at room temperature
• l tablespoon sake
l tablespoon usukuchi shoyu
• ½ teaspoon flaky sea salt
• 4 tablespoons
panko
6 tablespoons canola (rapeseed) oil
· 2 sheets
nori
PAN-FRIED FISH BALLS
Fish balls are tricky : They can end
up either too dry or too mushy.
Adding flour helps control the
texture, and pan-frying renders
them appealingly crunchy on the
surface . The aromatics add a bright
note to these savory bites. Serve
hot before dinner with a crisp
white wine.
Slice the fillets lengthwise into
strips and then crosswise into
a rough dice. Chop well on a
cutting board with a flat-bladed
sharp knife . Scrape into a
suribachi
[grinding bowl] and process to a
paste. (Alternatively , pulse in a
food processor.) Fold in the shiso,
ginger, scallion (spring onion) ,
sesame seeds , and miso. Mix until
all of the ingredients are well
incorporated. Sift in the flour
to stiffen the paste a little.
Set a small bowl of water next to
your workspace , dampen your
palms, and form 12 balls . Roll
the
balls in flour, shake off the excess,
and set the floured fish balls
on
a large dinner plate .
In a large frying pan, heat the oil
over medium-high heat until hot
but not smoking. Fry the balls,
turning periodically , until evenly
browned, 5-7 minutes. Remove the
cooked fish balls
to a clean dinner
plate lined with a piece of attractively
foldedJapanese calligraphy paper
(washi). Fry the reserved fish bones
in
the oil. Arrange the fried bones
on the plate along with the fish balls.
FRIED CHICKEN MEATBALLS
WITH NORI
There are myriad chicken meatball
recipes floating around Japan.
This one can be Westernized by
squeezing a little lemon juice
on top before serving and using
chopped parsley in place of nori.
Great for a passed canape at
cocktail
parties.
Fill a medium pot halfway with
water and add the fine salt.
Drop
the carrot into the water, bring
to a boil over high heat, and cook
until half done, about 5 minutes.
Drain, cool , and finely dice.
In a bowl, mix together the
chicken , carrot, shiitake, negi, egg ,
sake, usukuchi sh'!)lu, flaky sea salt , and
panko with a wooden spoon. Form
24 small
meatballs , about I heaping
tablespoon mixture per ball.
In a large heavy frying pan ,
heat the oil over medium heat.
Working in two batches, cook the
meatballs , turning frequently , for
2-3 minutes , until all surfaces
have lightly browned. Reduce the
heat to low , cover, and cook
2 more
minutes, shaking the pan
gently. Uncover , return the heat
to medium , and cook another
minute , while tilting the pan to
roll the balls for even cooking
and coloring. Drain on absorbent
paper towels .
To serve, crumble the nori over
the meatballs and serve hot with
a cocktail pick stuck into each
meatball .
251 AGEMONO
- FRIED

recipes.title: Chicken Terrine Tsoyupin 255 Yakimono - Grilled
recipes.transcription:
Preparation time, 25 minutes
Cooking time, 30
minutes
Makes, 2 small
terrines
I teaspoon canola (rapeseed) oil
• I small carrot, scrubbed
2 dried
shiitake , soaked in I cup
(8 fl oz/250 ml) boiling water for
30 minutes
2½ oz (75 g) freshly boiled or vacuum­
packed bamboo shoot , finely diced
2 tablespoons
finely chopped negi or
scallion (spring onion)
I egg, at room temperature
I tablespoon usukuchi shoyu
• I tablespoon sake
½ teaspoon fine sea salt
I lb 2 oz (500 g) finely ground
(minced) chicken
3 tablespoons
panko

warmed in a small, dry frying pan
Preparation time, 30
minutes plus
30 minutes resting time
Cooking time, IO minutes
Makes, 24 small pancakes
3 1/3 cups (17 1/2 oz/500 g) unbleached
bread (strong) flour
I teaspoon fine sea salt
I tablespoon gold sesame oil
2 tablespoons
gold sesame seeds , lightly
toasted in a small, dry frying pan
6 tablespoons finely chopped negi or
scallion (spring onion)

• Soy sauce, for dipping (optional)
CHICKEN TERRINE
Chicken loaves make a great little
cold bite on a {ensai plate (page
28) before dinner, but can also be
eaten warm . This loaf is baked, but
could easily be steamed instead.
Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C /
Gas
Mark 5). Line 2 (2-x 4-inch/
5 x IO cm) loaf pans with
parchment paper and rub the oil
on the bottom and sides of the
paper to make removal easier .
In a small pan of boiling water,
cook the carrot for 3 minutes.
Drain
and finely dice . Drain the
soaked shiitake, remove and discard
the stems, and finely chop the caps.
In a small bowl , whisk together
TSOYUPIN
These little fried pancakes get
their flakiness from the dough
that is laminated with sesame oil.
Although delicious, ts'!)'upin seem to
have fallen out of favor in current­
day Japan. Chinese in origin, these
are kn o wn as scallion pancakes in
the West.
In a large bowl , whisk together the
flour and salt. Mix in 'I• cup plus
r½ tablespoons (6 fl oz/200 ml)
water
with a pair of saibashi [cooking
chopsticks ). Knead the dough until
it resembles your soft earlobe to
the touch. Add water or flour as
necessary. Wet a cotton tea towe l,
squeeze out excess water, and wrap
the dough in the towel. Let rest in a
warm place for 20 - 30 minutes .
Divide the dough into 3 portions
and roll each into a ball , pulling
the bottoms of the dough together
to make them taut. Working with
one at a time, roll out a ball into a
large round. Brush with one-third
of the sesame oil and sprinkle with
one-third of the sesame seeds and
the egg, usukuchi sh'!)'u, sake, and
salt. In a separate bowl , combine
the chicken, carrot , shiitake,
bamboo shoot, negi, panko, black
sesame seeds, and egg mixture
until all of the ingredients are
well incorporated . Pack into the
parchment-lined loaf pans and
smooth the tops.
Bake in the center of the oven for
20 minutes until whitened and set.
Let rest in the pans for 5 minutes,
run a knife around the edges, and
unm o ld onto a cutting board. Cool
5 more minutes before cutting . Eat
warm, at room temperature,
or chilled .
negi. Starting from the side closest
to you , roll the round into a log.
Cut the dough log crosswise into
eight r¼-inch (3 cm) lengths. Roll
each of those pieces into 4-inch
(ro

the remaining balls of dough to
make 24 pancakes.
In
a large frying pan, heat
2 tablespoons of the canola
(rapeseed) oil over medium-high
heat. Working in batches, fry the
pancakes until golden brown on
each side, about 30 seconds per
side . Repeat with the remaining
pancakes, adding more oil as
needed . Cut into quarters to serve,
as is, or with a small saucer of soy
sauce, for dipping.
